sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: What is the primary benefit of regular physical education classes in school?
options: A) Reducing the need to study other subjects
B) Improving overall physical, mental, and social well-being
D) Allowing students to sleep better during class
questions.answer: B) Improving overall physical, mental, and social well-being

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered a track event in Athletics?
questions.answer: C) 100m Sprint

questions.question_text: The ability of a joint to move through its complete and full range of motion is called:
questions.answer: C) Flexibility

questions.question_text: Which fundamental motor skill involves propelling an object away from the body using the hand and arm?
questions.answer: B) Throwing

questions.question_text: True or False: Cardiovascular endurance can be improved by short, 10-second bursts of running.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: In a long jump event, what is the crucial phase where the athlete leaves the ground called?
questions.answer: C) Take-off

questions.question_text: What does BMI (Body Mass Index) primarily help to estimate?
options: C) Body fat based on height and weight
questions.answer: C) Body fat based on height and weight

questions.question_text: Which of these activities relies most heavily on the fitness component of 'Balance'?
options: A) Walking across a narrow balance beam
B) Lifting a heavy weight once
questions.answer: A) Walking across a narrow balance beam

questions.question_text: The shuttle run test is primarily designed to measure which component of motor fitness?
questions.answer: B) Agility and speed

questions.question_text: True or False: A proper warm-up before athletic events decreases the risk of muscle injuries.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Why is performing a cool-down routine important after finishing an intense athletic workout? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A cool-down helps gradually lower the heart rate back to a normal resting state. It also prevents muscle stiffness and reduces the buildup of lactic acid.

questions.question_text: State the main difference between muscular strength and muscular endurance. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Muscular strength is the maximum force a muscle can exert in a single effort, while endurance is the ability to sustain repeated muscle contractions over time.

questions.question_text: List any two fundamental locomotor skills used in track and field events. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Two fundamental locomotor skills commonly used in track and field are sprinting (running fast over short distances) and leaping (jumping forward from one foot to another).

questions.question_text: How does improving physical fitness positively affect a student's mental well-being? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Physical fitness reduces stress and anxiety by releasing endorphins in the brain. It also improves focus, confidence, and promotes better sleep habits for students.

questions.question_text: Name the piece of equipment passed between runners during a relay race and state one rule regarding it. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The equipment is called a baton. A key rule is that the baton must be passed within the designated exchange zone without being dropped.

questions.question_text: Explain the three main phases of a successful long jump: the approach, take-off, and landing. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The approach involves a fast, controlled run to build momentum. The take-off requires driving forcefully off the board with one foot to gain height. The landing involves bringing both feet forward and falling forward into the sandpit to maximize distance.

questions.question_text: Describe a simple physical test you can perform at school to measure the flexibility of your lower back and hamstrings. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The Sit-and-Reach test measures flexibility. A student sits on the floor with legs straight against a box. Keeping knees flat, they reach forward along a measuring scale on top of the box as far as possible without bending their knees.

questions.question_text: What is 'reaction time' in sports, and why is it crucial for a sprinter waiting at the starting line? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Reaction time is the speed at which a person responds to a stimulus. For a sprinter, a fast reaction time to the sound of the starting gun is crucial because a quicker start provides an immediate advantage in a short race.

questions.question_text: How does maintaining good cardiovascular endurance benefit an individual in their daily life, outside of playing sports? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Good cardiovascular endurance means the heart and lungs work efficiently. In daily life, this allows a person to climb stairs, walk long distances, or carry groceries without getting easily exhausted or out of breath, improving overall energy levels.

questions.question_text: A student complains of frequent leg cramps and fatigue during the second half of a long-distance run. Analyze what components of fitness they lack and suggest a structured training and hydration plan to help them improve. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The student likely lacks muscular endurance and cardiovascular stamina, and may be suffering from dehydration. To improve, they should practice continuous, moderate-paced jogging to build lung capacity and stamina. Additionally, they must implement a strict hydration plan, drinking water before, during, and after runs to prevent severe muscle cramping and premature fatigue.

questions.question_text: During physical education class, the teacher emphasizes the mechanics of throwing a ball accurately. Break down the correct biomechanical steps—stance, arm motion, weight transfer, and follow-through—required to throw a ball powerfully and accurately at a target. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: First, the student must adopt a sideways stance facing the target. The throwing arm is drawn back while pointing the non-throwing arm at the target. During the throw, the student shifts body weight from the back foot to the front foot, rotating the hips forward. Finally, the arm follows through across the body to ensure maximum power and pinpoint accuracy.
